features.notes: control.flags (VERBOSE, EXCLUSIVE) exist but are never read. Terminal sets and excluded members accumulate until the DB is wiped and are replicated in full to new peers.

features.name: Quiesce set and member state machine
features.summary: Derives each member's and each set's state from the acknowledgements of all member ranks.
features.description: State values (as encoded): INVALID 0, QUIESCING 1, QUIESCED 2, RELEASING 3, RELEASED 4, EXPIRED 5, FAILED 6, CANCELED 7 and TIMEDOUT 8 (the last two for sets only); aggregation uses min and max, so the order is part of the semantics. For each member the leader takes every peer's (including its own) last reported state, defaulting to the requested state when a peer reported nothing for the root; a reported EXPIRED or FAILED is adopted by the member and the set, a lower effective state rolls the member back (for example QUIESCED to QUIESCING when a new rank joins), and otherwise the member advances only when every peer has acked the current {epoch, set version}. The set follows the minimum member state, except that a RELEASING set counts reports of QUIESCED or RELEASED as RELEASED. Agents are asked for QUIESCING while a set is QUIESCING or QUIESCED and for RELEASING while it is RELEASING.
features.notes: A member is QUIESCED only when every member rank reports it quiesced. Every MDSMap epoch change makes all acks stale until each agent acks the new epoch (one round trip per map change). Adding a rank during a quiesce rolls QUIESCED members back and restarts their timeout.

features.name: Quiesce timeout and expiration
features.summary: Bounds how long a set may take to become quiesced and how long it may stay quiesced.
features.description: timeout (per set, applied to each member) runs from the member's inclusion, reset or rollback: a QUIESCING member with at_age + timeout <= now makes the set TIMEDOUT, leaving the member state unchanged. expiration bounds the time in QUIESCED or RELEASING, measured from reaching QUIESCED and restarted by each successful quiesce-await; when it elapses the set becomes EXPIRED, and a release keeps at_age so the expiration clock keeps running. Both default to 0: a new set without a timeout is TIMEDOUT on the first leader pass, and a QUIESCED set with expiration 0 expires right after its awaits complete. All times are ages relative to the leader's time_zero (coarse_real_clock, unsigned 64-bit nanoseconds), and replicas set time_zero = now - db_age from each listing, so clocks need not be synchronized.
features.notes: --release ignores --timeout and --expiration (they are applied only in the non-release branch), although doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:1740-1743 says any command to an active set may update them. A backwards wall-clock step before time_zero underflows get_age, and TTLs use non-saturating addition (code reading).

features.name: Quiesce await semantics
features.summary: Lets a request wait until its set is QUIESCED (or RELEASED for a release), with a defined error code for every other outcome.
features.description: --await (unbounded) or --await-for <secs> keeps a request pending after its update. A pending quiesce-await completes with 0 when the set is QUIESCED (and then restarts the expiration clock), EPERM on RELEASING or RELEASED, ECANCELED on CANCELED, ETIMEDOUT on EXPIRED or TIMEDOUT, EBADF on FAILED, ENOENT if the set vanished, EINPROGRESS when the await interval elapses or leadership is lost, and EINTR (or ECANCELED) when another request changes the set's members; a release-await completes with 0 on RELEASED. A quiesce-await submitted on a set already beyond QUIESCED returns EPERM at once. Awaits on QUIESCED and RELEASED are completed before the expiration check of the same pass, so with expiration 0 a quiesce-await still succeeds ("barriers").
features.notes: --cancel --await returns EPERM after a successful cancel (documented in fs-volumes.rst). Release-await success means every member rank has killed its quiesce ops; parked requests are retried and caps re-issued asynchronously afterwards, so client I/O may resume slightly later.

features.name: Quiesce if_version optimistic concurrency
features.summary: Makes a quiesce request conditional on the set's current version.
features.description: With --if-version N on an existing set the request fails with ESTALE unless N equals the set's version; if_version 0 therefore fails on any existing set and works as create-only. if_version > 0 without a set id gives EINVAL. Every set change sets the set's version to db.set_version + 1 (several changes in one leader pass share a version), and the reply shows the DB set_version and each set's version.

features.name: Quiesce root URI sanitization
features.summary: Normalizes quiesce roots to file:/path or inode:N before storing them.
features.description: Each root is parsed as a URI reference and normalized; no scheme means file, and any scheme other than file or inode gives EINVAL. An authority must equal the fs name or the numeric fs id and is then removed; repeated slashes collapse, trailing slashes are dropped, file: paths get a leading /, and inode: paths must be a canonical non-zero decimal uint64. Members are stored and reported in this form (for example file:/volumes/_nogroup/sub1/<uuid>), which is visible in the JSON reply.
features.notes: Numeric fs-id authorities are rejected because the MDS never fills in fs_id (only the literal -1 matches). inode: roots are accepted by the DB, but the agent turns them into a relative path with base ino 0, so path_traverse returns -ESTALE and the member becomes FAILED (code reading). Tests: src/test/mds/TestQuiesceDb.cc:620-727 (RootSanitization).

features.name: Quiesce DB replication between ranks
features.summary: The leader replicates set changes to every member rank and collects their per-root acknowledgements.
features.description: MMDSQuiesceDbListing (MSG_MDS_QUIESCE_DB_LISTING 0x505, payload {origin gid, {db_version{epoch u32, set_version u64}, db_age u64 ns, sets}}) goes from the leader to each peer with the sets newer than the peer's last ack, at most once per second per peer and only during leader passes (no idle retransmission). MMDSQuiesceDbAck (0x506, payload {origin gid, diff map tagged with the processed DB version}) goes from each agent to the leader and lists only roots whose actual state differs from the requested one. A replica rejects listings whose epoch differs from its membership epoch (ESTALE) and discards its whole DB on a lower set_version. A new leader, and an existing leader when a member joins, first sends discovery listings (set_version 0, every 1 s) to unknown peers, adopts the highest uploaded DB (with set_version + 1) and processes no request, ack or timer until all of them answered; there is no timeout. All structs are ENCODE_START(1,1) envelopes and are MDS-to-MDS only.
features.notes: quiesce_dispatch runs before the stale-message check and the peer-type filter, and the manager trusts the payload origin (only membership is checked). A listing a replica rejected for epoch skew is not requested again; it arrives only with a later leader pass. A silent member blocks a bootstrapping leader until membership changes (code reading).

features.name: Per-rank quiesce agent
features.summary: Each active rank turns the replicated DB into quiesce or release actions on its own cache and reports the actual state per root.
features.description: After each DB change the manager computes a root-centric quiesce map from active sets (root -> {requested state, ttl}; a root in several sets gets the minimum state and maximum ttl; roots of terminal sets are absent, meaning release) and hands it to the agent thread mds-q-agt. For each root the agent submits one quiesce_path request when the root should be quiesced (under mds_lock; with a degraded MDSMap the root fails with EPERM), cancels it with request_kill when the root is releasing or disappears, and reports QUIESCED once the quiesce completed, RELEASED after a successful cancel, EXPIRED when the cancel found no request or the result was lost, and FAILED on an error. Acks are sent asynchronously and are delivered locally on the leader; the reported TTL is never acted on.
features.notes: Agents of different ranks act independently; the only cross-rank coupling is the leader's min-over-ranks aggregation. A root is acked QUIESCED in the pass that cancels it, which the leader maps to RELEASED for a releasing set.

features.name: Quiesce on degraded file systems and non-active ranks
features.summary: Cancels all active sets while the file system is degraded and keeps non-active ranks from quiescing.
features.description: When the MDSMap is degraded (failed or damaged ranks, or any daemon in REPLAY..CLIENTREPLAY) and this MDS is the leader, quiesce_cluster_update injects a cancel-all request at the front of the queue on every map epoch, and agents refuse new quiesces with EPERM (reported as FAILED) until the file system is healthy. A rank that is not up:active replaces its agent callback with a responder that reports QUIESCING roots as FAILED if the map is degraded, QUIESCED if the rank is standby-replay, and otherwise drops them, and resets its agent asynchronously (all roots dropped, all quiesce requests cancelled). Leaving membership wipes the local DB.
features.notes: With the current monitor rule non-active ranks are never members, so the responder is dormant except in a short window between reset_agent_callback and update_membership (code reading; not observed in tests).

features.name: Tree quiesce request (quiesce_path)
features.summary: An internal request that quiesces everything under one root on this rank and holds the quiesce until it is killed.
features.description: MDCache::quiesce_path starts internal op CEPH_MDS_OP_QUIESCE_PATH (0x01508, name quiesce_path). dispatch_quiesce_path answers -EAGAIN unless the rank is up:active, traverses with DISCOVER, RDLOCK_PATH and WANT_INODE (discovering missing components from their auth ranks and keeping rdlocks on every path dentry), ends with the traverse error (for example -ENOENT, or -ENOTDIR for an intermediate symlink), completes at once for a non-auth root when mds_cache_quiesce_splitauth is false, and otherwise starts a quiesce_inode op for the root. When the root and, transitively, all its cached descendants are quiesced, it completes its finisher with 0 but is not finished: it keeps its path locks and owns all child quiesce_inode ops until request_kill. A failure recorded by any child fails the whole request.
features.notes: Admin entry point for a local tree quiesce: quiesce path (F-ADM-053).

features.name: Per-inode quiesce request (quiesce_inode)
features.summary: An internal request per cached inode that takes the inode's quiesce locks, forces cap revocation and recurses into cached children.
features.description: CEPH_MDS_OP_QUIESCE_INODE (0x01509) acquires with skip_quiesce an xlock on quiescelock and an rdlock on policylock (both kept for the whole quiesce) and, on the auth, a filelock xlock plus authlock, linklock and xattrlock rdlocks; with splitauth (default) the auth drops the cap-related locks after acquisition, without it the rdlocks are kept and a non-auth dirfrag fails with -EPERM. The filelock xlock passes through states that allow only Fc and Fb, revoking Fs, Fr, Fw, Fx and Fl while leaving cached reads and buffered dirty data, and the rdlocks revoke Ax, Lx and Xx, so acquisition waits for clients to acknowledge the revocations. For a directory it starts a child op for every cached head dentry not yet visited and completes only after all children completed (bottom-up); uncached inodes are not walked. An inode already quiesced by another op makes the request return -EINPROGRESS, which fails the path (nested roots in different sets, duplicate quiesce path).
features.notes: QA checks that each completed quiesce_inode holds exactly iquiesce (x) and ipolicy (r), plus the cap-lock rdlocks without splitauth, and that no client holds Ax, Lx, Xx, Fx or Fw (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quiesce.py:229-318). Every quiesced inode costs one MDRequest plus held locks and cannot be trimmed; replica copies are not auth-pinned. An unresponsive client stalls the quiesce until it is evicted or the set times out.

features.name: quiescelock and parking of mutations
features.summary: A per-inode local lock whose xlock by a quiesce op makes new write and exclusive locks of cap-related locks wait.
features.description: CInode::quiescelock is a local lock of type CEPH_LOCK_IQUIESCE (1<<4, the lowest inode lock type, name iquiesce), not replicated: each rank has its own. A wrlock is allowed only when it is not xlocked and no xlock is waiting (writer preference for the quiesce); an xlock needs no wrlocks. Unless skip_quiesce is passed, Locker::acquire_locks adds a quiescelock wrlock for the inode of the first xlock, wrlock or remote wrlock of a cap-related lock (IAUTH, ILINK, IFILE, IXATTR) in the caller's lock list, at most one per call, sorted before that inode's other locks; rdlocks never add it. If the quiescelock cannot be taken, the request drops all its locks (local and remote) and auth pins and waits (op event "failed to acquire quiesce lock"), so that it does not hold the parent snaplock and policylock rdlocks that mksnap needs. On release, waiters are woken before caps are re-evaluated. skip_quiesce is used by quiesce_inode, lock path, export locking, the quarantine root op and peer OP_XLOCK/OP_WRLOCK from a leader rank.
features.notes: Blocked while quiesced: create, mknod, mkdir, symlink, link, unlink, rmdir and rename in quiesced directories, setattr, O_TRUNC opens, user xattr changes and vxattrs needing a policylock xlock. Proceeding: getattr, lookup, readdir, open without truncation, mksnap, cap-snap and dirty-data flushes, fcntl/flock locks. Only the first cap-related wr/xlock of a call gets the implicit wrlock, while doc/dev/mds_internals/quiesce.rst says every such lock does; a multi-inode operation whose first cap-related lock is outside the quiesced tree could still wrlock a quiesced directory's filelock (cross-subvolume renames fail with EXDEV, narrowing this; code reading, untested). See also F-CAPS-081 (lock-acquisition details), F-CAPS-066 (local lock type).

features.name: Cap masking while quiesced
features.summary: Limits the caps issued on a quiesced inode to read, cache, buffer and pin, so clients cannot start new writes or take exclusive caps.
features.description: While CInode::is_quiesced() (quiescelock xlocked by a quiesce_inode op), get_caps_quiesce_mask = CEPH_CAP_ANY_RD | Fc | Fb | p (that is p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc Fb) is ANDed into the liked, allowed-by-type (hence Locker::get_allowed_caps and InodeStat caps), careful, xlocker and wanted masks, so lock state machines do not move toward EXCL or MIX. Clients keep Fb and can still flush dirty data and cap updates (an Fb holder can still get max_size raised), but writes, fallocate and copy_file_range wait in the client for Fw. Lock-cache cap bits are added only when Fx is allowed and taking the quiescelock xlock invalidates existing lock caches, so kernel async creates and unlinks fall back to synchronous requests, which park.
features.notes: An xlock taken by "lock path quiesce:x" blocks mutations but does not mask caps. Kernel ceph_write_iter needs Fw (linux/fs/ceph/file.c:2477); libcephfs Client::_write waits in Client::get_caps; for NFS-Ganesha, worker threads block (inferred). Revoking Fw while keeping Fb avoids forced write-back, which the code comment says could make the quiesce time out.

features.name: Quiescing inodes that appear during a quiesce
features.summary: Quiesces inodes that are linked into an already-quiesced directory after the walk passed it.
features.description: CDir::link_inode_work, run whenever a primary inode is linked into a dirfrag (dirfrag fetch, replica decode, import, rejoin, projected-linkage application), calls MDCache::add_quiesce if the directory inode is quiesced; add_quiesce starts a quiesce_inode op for the head child under the same quiesce_path request, with a no-op finisher outside any gather. For example, find on a quiesced subvolume after a cache drop quiesces every loaded inode (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quiesce.py:579-612).

features.name: Quiesce and directory fragmentation
features.summary: Keeps fragmentation from deadlocking with or escaping a quiesce.
features.description: MDCache::can_fragment refuses split and merge of a quiesced directory. For each dirfrag a quiesce_inode walks, and whenever the quiesce_path traverse must wait, quiesce_overdrive_fragmenting_async aborts a live fragment operation on that dirfrag that is not yet fully frozen; dispatch_fragment_dir then requeues the split or merge, unfreezes and finishes. dispatch_fragment_dir also aborts itself if the directory inode would block on the quiescelock before it takes its locks, because blocking with frozen dirfrags would deadlock with quiesce ops waiting on them. Quiesced auth inodes keep their auth pins, so freezes that cover them cannot complete until release.
features.notes: QA exercises merge/split churn during quiesce (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quiesce.py:614-650). Fragmentation itself belongs to 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags. See also F-CACHE-093 (fragment op cancellation).

features.name: Quiesce and subtree migration
features.summary: Refuses or cancels subtree exports that touch a quiesced tree.
features.description: Migrator::export_dir refuses dirfrags whose inode is quiesced; quiesce_overdrive_export, called for every dirfrag a quiesce_inode walks, cancels an export of that dirfrag that is still at or before EXPORT_FREEZING; dispatch_export_dir cancels if the directory would block on the quiescelock (its own acquire_locks uses skip_quiesce). On the importer, path_traverse with MDS_TRAVERSE_IMPORT returns -EAGAIN instead of discovering below a quiesced non-auth directory and the importer NAKs the discover, so the exporter cancels; imported inodes under a quiesced parent are quiesced through add_quiesce. request_forward of an internal op completes it with -EXDEV.
features.notes: If the importer already has the base inode cached, no quiesce check is made. Subtree migration belongs to 07-multi-mds. See also F-MULTI-025.

features.name: Quiesce release and cancel cascade
features.summary: Releases a root by killing its quiesce_path request, which kills every child op and drops their locks.
features.description: The agent's cancel_request (under mds_lock) calls MDCache::request_kill on the quiesce_path request if it still exists and returns 0, otherwise ENOENT (the root is then reported EXPIRED instead of RELEASED). request_kill completes a still-pending finisher with -ECANCELED, and request_cleanup kills every op in the request's quiesce_ops (resetting the heartbeat every mds_heartbeat_reset_grace ops) and drops the path locks; each killed quiesce_inode drops its quiescelock xlock and policylock rdlock, which wakes parked requests and re-issues caps. A C_MDS_QuiescePath destroyed without finishing completes its finisher with -ECANCELED. On rank shutdown the agent is shut down with mds_lock released and the manager joins its thread.

features.name: Quiesce dispatch throttle and heartbeat resets
features.summary: Rate-limits quiesce_inode dispatch and keeps the daemon heartbeat alive during large walks.
features.description: Before taking locks each quiesce_inode checks quiesce_counter, a DecayCounter with half-life mds_cache_quiesce_decay_rate (1 s): above mds_cache_quiesce_threshold (512K) it retries after mds_cache_quiesce_sleep (200 ms) on the timer, otherwise it records a hit. mds_cache_quiesce_delay (dev, 0 ms) delays the root op and each child op, and heartbeat_reset is called every mds_heartbeat_reset_grace (1000) dispatched or killed quiesce ops. The three throttle options are applied at runtime through MDCache::handle_conf_change; splitauth and delay are read on every dispatch_quiesce_path. The DB protocol uses hard-coded constants: discovery interval 1 s (+100 ms), repeated-update interval 1 s, maximum db thread wait 10 s.

features.name: ceph.quiesce.block vxattr
features.summary: A persistent per-inode flag that exempts an inode, and for a directory its whole subtree, from quiesce.
features.description: Setting ceph.quiesce.block (a bool) requires MAY_SET_VXATTR, xlocks policylock and snaplock, projects inode_t::flags |= F_QUIESCE_BLOCK (1<<1) and journals it without early reply; the flag is persisted with the inode (inode_t v16+ flags) and is read back with getvxattr. A quiesce_inode op that finds the flag drops its locks but keeps its auth pins, counts inodes_blocked, completes with 0 and does not recurse, so a blocked directory exempts its whole subtree. Setting the flag waits for any active quiesce of the inode (policylock xlock versus the quiesce's rdlock). Clients reach it through the generic ceph.* xattr passthrough (kernel SETXATTR and GETVXATTR).
features.notes: Shown as quiesce_block in inode dumps and qblock in inode prints. Virtual xattr handling in general belongs to 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

features.name: quiesce db command
features.summary: The admin and mgr entry point to the quiesce DB; the leader answers with a JSON listing of sets.
features.description: "quiesce db [<roots>...] [--set-id] [--timeout] [--expiration] [--await-for|--await] [--if-version] [--include|--exclude|--reset|--release|--query|--cancel] [--all]" is registered for asok and tell (tell needs allow *) and runs without mds_lock. More than one op, release or cancel with roots, cancel without --set-id or --all, reset without set id or roots, and query with roots give -EINVAL; no op means include (query when no roots are given); durations are float seconds. The reply is always json-pretty {epoch, leader, set_version, sets: {<id>: {version, age_ref, state{name, age}, timeout, expiration, members{<root>: {excluded, state{name, age}}}}}}, holding the requested set (also on error), all sets for a query without id, nothing for cancel-all, and no inactive sets other than the requested one unless --all. A non-member or non-leader answers -ENOTTY with {epoch, leader} from its MDSMap so that the caller can retry at the leader; otherwise the return code is the negated errno with an empty status string.
features.notes: After a demotion the reply's leader is the answering MDS itself, so the mgr retry returns to the same MDS, which then answers with the map's leader (bounded by 5 retries). The JSON layout, state names, member key format (file:/path), set id format and error codes are user-visible API documented in doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:1625-2033. Without a quiesce DB manager the command returns -EFAULT. Error codes returned in the reply as negated errnos: EINVAL, ENOENT, EPERM, ESTALE, EINPROGRESS, ETIMEDOUT, ECANCELED, EINTR, EBADF, ENOTTY; the leader replies from thread mds-q-db. Command plane: F-ADM-054; mgr/volumes caller: F-ADM-101. See also F-ADM-101 (mgr/volumes fs quiesce).

features.name: Quiesce observability: counters and op events
features.summary: Exposes quiesce progress through two request counters and op events in dump_ops_in_flight.
features.description: The mds_cache perf counters ireq_quiesce_path and ireq_quiesce_inode count finished or killed quiesce_path and quiesce_inode requests. dump_ops_in_flight shows quiesce ops with flag points such as "quiescing root", "quiescing children", "quiesce complete", "quiesce complete for non-auth inode", "quiesce complete for non-auth tree", "quiesce blocked" and "failed to acquire quiesce lock", plus the locks they hold; QA asserts on four of them (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quiesce.py:124-127). There are no gauges for active sets, quiesced inodes or parked requests and no health warnings; the log subsystem is mds_quiesce.

features.name: quarantine enable and disable commands
features.summary: Admin commands that mark or unmark one subvolume root as quarantined and reply when the operation has completed.
features.description: "quarantine enable path=<abs path>" and "quarantine disable path=<abs path>" (asok and tell; tell needs allow *) start internal op CEPH_MDS_OP_QUARANTINEDIR_AUTH, which resolves the path wanting auth and requires a subvolume root (a directory whose snaprealm's subvolume ino is itself: v2 subvolume roots, not <uuid> data directories, groups or files). The reply comes after the root's flag change is journaled and the local cap walk is done: JSON {return_code, operation: "enable"|"disable", status: "successful"|"failed"[, error]} with result 0 (done, or already in the requested state with nothing journaled), -EINVAL (not a subvolume root), -EBUSY (another operation on the root in flight), -ENOENT (path missing or root vanished), -EXDEV (this rank is not auth for the root; there is no forwarding) or -ECANCELED (op killed). A daemon without a rank returns mds_not_active.
features.notes: A relative or empty path resolves through base ino 0 and is expected to end in -ESTALE after a RADOS round trip (unverified at runtime). A rank that is not active (replay, standby-replay, rejoin) also starts the operation and would assert in MDLog if it reached the journal (inferred, untested). Introduced May-Oct 2026 (44 commits). The internal op code is CEPH_MDS_OP_QUARANTINEDIR_AUTH (0x150c); the command runs under mds_lock and its rc equals return_code. The inode's authority follows the dirfrag holding its dentry, so -EXDEV comes from the rank that is not auth for that dirfrag. Command plane: F-ADM-055; mgr/volumes caller: F-ADM-102. See also F-ADM-102 (mgr/volumes quarantine command).

features.name: Persistent quarantine flag in inode optmetadata
features.summary: Stores quarantine state as an optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE on the subvolume root inode, journaled with an EUpdate.
features.description: The flag is an inode_t::optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE = 2 holding quarantine_md_t (ENCODE_START(1,1): bool enabled, u64 quarantined_at_sec, u32 quarantined_at_nsec); has_quarantined() means the entry exists with enabled true, and disable removes the entry. The optmetadata container is ENCODE_START(1,1) plus a vector of {u64 kind, payload in its own envelope} kept sorted by kind, with kinds above 3 kept as opaque blobs; it is carried in inode_t encoding v20+, InodeStat v8+ and policylock payload v4. MDCache::quarantine_inode xlocks the root's authlock, linklock, xattrlock, filelock, snaplock and policylock (skip_quiesce), projects set_quarantine or del_quarantine together with change_attr++, ctime = now and an rctime update, and journals EUpdate "quarantine flag add" or "quarantine flag del" (root inode plus its primary dentry) without early reply. The flag survives restart and failover through ordinary metablob replay; there is no FSMap or MDSMap state, no RADOS object of its own, no config option and no perf counter.
features.notes: optmetadata kind 3 (equal to _MAX) is mishandled: get_kind tests > instead of >=, indexing one past the table (undefined behaviour, code reading). Enable and disable change the root's ctime, change_attr (NFSv4 change attribute) and rctime. The real quarantined_at is visible only through dump inode. The optmetadata container is shared with charmap (kind 1); inode encoding belongs to 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags and 06-journal-and-storage.

features.name: In-progress quarantine state and operation ordering
features.summary: Marks the subvolume root in memory as being quarantined or unquarantined, so that enforcement starts or stops before the flag is journaled.
features.description: After validation the auth rank sets CInode::quarantine_op on the subvolume root (NONE 0, ADD 1, DEL 2); the journal finisher or an abort clears it. The enforcement predicate treats ADD as quarantined and DEL as not quarantined, so enforcement starts when an enable is accepted and stops when a disable is accepted, before the EUpdate is safe; a crash in between reverts to the persisted state. The operation then queues a QUARANTINEDIR_WORK op on the finisher, which queues the QUARANTINE_INODE op for the root (flag change and journal) and starts the cap-revocation walk; the command replies only after both complete. Replica ranks never see quarantine_op.

features.name: Per-subvolume quarantine operation registry
features.summary: Allows at most one enable or disable per subvolume root at a time on a rank and rejects concurrent ones with EBUSY.
features.description: MDSRank::qtine_ops maps subvolume root inode numbers to a QuarantineTracker under qtine_mutex; register_quarantine_mgr fails with -EBUSY while a non-complete tracker exists and replaces a complete one. The tracker counts two work items (root flag journal, local walk) with add_work, seal and work_done (which fires the callback with 0 once sealed and pending reaches 0) and complete(r) (which fires it at once); the callback fires at most once, unregisters the root, undoes on error and sends the JSON reply. The internal ops are created "continuous", which exempts them from slow-op warnings, and print as ??? in dump_ops_in_flight.
features.notes: Killing the QUARANTINE_INODE op with op kill leaves the command unanswered, the registry entry busy (-EBUSY for that subvolume until restart) and quarantine_op set. The same happens if the root stops being auth on this rank between validation and quarantine_inode (inferred, untested race). The tracker refcount and statistics are never read; QuarantineManager.cc is empty.

features.name: Quarantine undo on failure
features.summary: Clears the in-progress mark and wakes parked requests when an enable or disable fails.
features.description: abort_quarantine_op(ino, op) runs from the tracker callback when r < 0 and the tracker was registered: it clears quarantine_op if it still equals op and calls finish_waiting(WAIT_QUARANTINE) on the root so that parked requests retry. Failures before registration (missing path, not a subvolume root, -EBUSY, -EXDEV) have nothing to undo; a root or tracker that vanished in later steps completes with -ENOENT and aborts. A failed or cancelled walk (for example -EAGAIN in up:clientreplay) is ignored: the command reports success without proactive cap revocation. The journal write cannot fail in this path (C_MDS_inode_update_finish asserts r == 0).
features.notes: Requests that parked in rdlock_path_pin_ref or rdlock_path_xlock_dentry are not re-checked when woken (PATH_LOCKED), so a wake-up by the abort of a failed disable lets them proceed although the flag is still set.

features.name: Quarantine cap-revocation walk
features.summary: Walks the subvolume tree on each rank and re-evaluates caps on every cached inode, so that the restriction takes effect, or is lifted, at once.
features.description: start_quarantine_cap_revocation starts a quiesce_path request on filepath(root ino) in quarantine mode (a non-auth root is walked regardless of splitauth). Each quiesce_inode in quarantine mode takes no locks and skips the quiesce throttle: unless the inode is the .meta file directly under the subvolume root, it runs Locker::eval and, if that issued nothing, Locker::issue_caps, which recomputes caps with the quarantine mask; on disable it also sends MQuarantineDisable to quarantine-aware cap holders and wakes WAIT_QUARANTINE waiters; for a directory it recurses into auth dirfrags only. When the root op finishes, the walk's quiesce_path request is killed from the finisher; the auth's completion ignores the result. On the auth the walk starts before the flag is journaled.
features.notes: Coverage gap: each rank descends only through dirfrags it is auth for, so inodes in a subtree delegated to another rank below a dirfrag of this rank are visited by neither walk; their caps are masked only at their next issue_caps (requests are still gated). Directories with visited children are processed twice (second eval and second MQuarantineDisable). A fully cached tree is typically walked recursively inside one mds_lock hold (inferred).

features.name: Quarantine propagation to replica ranks
features.summary: Carries the quarantine flag to other ranks through ordinary policylock replication and starts a local walk there.
features.description: quarantine_inode xlocks replicated locks, so the auth sends LOCK_AC_LOCK and gathers LOCKACKs (a replica acks only after its local rdlocks on the lock are released); for snaplock and policylock xlocks while the cluster is degraded with a replica rank below active, acquisition waits for full recovery. Releasing the xlock sends LOCK_AC_SYNC with the policylock payload v4, which includes optmetadata; the replica's decode_lock_ipolicy detects a change of has_quarantined on a subvolume root and calls handle_quarantine_policy_update, which starts a local walk whose completion nobody waits for. The auth replies without waiting for replicas, and a replica serves the subvolume normally until it processes LOCK_AC_SYNC.
features.notes: This replaced dedicated MMDSQuarantine messages, EQuarantineStart/Finish/Cancel events and op 0x0150d (commit 24d79f3a038). Requests parked on a replica hold rdlocks on its root snaplock and are woken only by that replica's DEL walk, which needs the auth's xlock, so a disable can wedge until those clients are evicted (inferred, untested).

features.name: Subtree export refused inside a quarantined subvolume
features.summary: Prevents migrating subtrees rooted at or inside a quarantined subvolume.
features.description: Migrator::export_dir silently refuses an export whose root dirfrag's inode is under quarantine (the subvolume root's own dirfrags and every dirfrag inside), also during up:stopping, so balancer exports, export pins and rank shutdown of such subtrees wait until the quarantine is lifted. An export rooted at an ancestor dirfrag (for example /volumes/<group>) is not refused and carries the subvolume root and nested dirfrags along; the persisted flag travels with the inode, the in-memory quarantine_op does not (inferred, untested).
features.notes: QA tear-down disables quarantine and removes export pins before reducing max_mds (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_quarantine.py:1105-1155). See also F-MULTI-025.

features.name: Quarantine re-enforcement after restart
features.summary: Applies the quarantine cap mask again to all reconnected caps when a rank becomes active.
features.description: The persisted flag is restored by replaying the EUpdate metablob or loaded from the parent dirfrag; quarantine_op and the operation registry start empty, and there is no quarantine-specific replay code. MDSRank::active_start calls MDCache::reissue_all_caps, which runs eval and issue_caps for every inode with caps and so applies the quarantine mask to caps that clients reconnected with. Standby-replay daemons replay the same EUpdate. An operation interrupted before its EUpdate was safe leaves the flag unchanged and has to be retried by the administrator.

features.name: Quarantine enforcement predicate
features.summary: Decides for any inode whether it lies inside a quarantined subvolume.
features.description: CInode::is_under_quarantine walks the snaprealm chain from the inode: for each realm's subvolume ino (the outermost enclosing subvolume), if that inode is cached it returns false when a disable is in flight, and true when an enable is in flight or the persisted flag is set; if the subvolume root is not cached it returns false (fail-open); otherwise it continues with the parent realm and returns false at the root realm. Coverage is every inode whose realm chain reaches the root, including snapshot views (.snap) at any depth. It runs on hot paths (every check_access, every Locker::issue_caps, which also builds the inode's full path to check q/Q, every encode_inodestat and loner changes) whether or not anything is quarantined.
features.notes: doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:1620-1622 says an uncached root fails closed; the code fails open (commit 630bf842c11). In practice the root is cached whenever a descendant is. Unlinked-but-open files in stray directories are outside the realm chain and not covered (inferred). Removing ceph.dir.subvolume from a quarantined root silently stops enforcement, and disable returns -EINVAL until the flag is set again.

features.name: MDS auth cap flags q and Q (quarantine access)
features.summary: Quarantine use of the q and Q MDS cap flags.
features.description: See F-ADM-015 for the flags. Quarantine-specific: the flags are consulted in two places, the per-request check for quarantine-aware sessions (F-QOS-071) and the cap restriction on every cap issue (F-QOS-074); neither is implied by allow *, so recovery clients need an explicit q or Q grant.
features.notes: The docs describe q as one quarantined path and Q as all; the code evaluates both identically, scoped by the grant's path and fsname.

features.name: Quarantine client feature bit 24
features.summary: Client feature bit that selects between EACCES enforcement (aware clients) and request parking (unaware clients).
features.description: CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE = 24, named "quarantine", is in CEPHFS_FEATURES_ALL, so the MDS and this release's libcephfs, ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha advertise it. The Linux kernel client snapshot neither defines nor advertises bit 24 and is always treated as unaware. The bit also decides who receives MQuarantineDisable, and its name is accepted wherever CephFS feature names are, for example fs required_client_features.
features.notes: Older libcephfs, ceph-fuse and Ganesha builds without bit 24 behave like the kernel client (their requests are parked). See also F-PROTO-021 (per-bit gated behaviour).

features.name: EACCES for quarantine-aware sessions
features.summary: Fails every metadata request of a quarantine-aware client without q/Q on an inode under quarantine with -EACCES.
features.description: Server::check_access sets check_qtine when the inode is under quarantine and the session has feature bit 24, and Session::check_access passes it to MDSAuthCaps::is_capable, whose false result becomes -EACCES. check_access runs in essentially every request handler on the target and/or parent inode (with mask 0 for lookups by ino), so all metadata operations of such clients inside the subvolume fail, including snapshot listing and a mount at a path inside it. Batched getattr and lookup followers skip the checks and inherit the batch head's result: success if the head has q, -EACCES (even for a q follower) if the head is an aware client without q, and an indefinite wait if the head is a parked unaware request.
features.notes: The C++ client's readdir tolerates -EACCES from _getattr on a quarantined child and uses cached attributes (commit 630bf842c11); I/O on an already-open file waits for caps instead of failing (code reading). Ganesha maps -EACCES to an NFS access error (inferred, untested). Renaming the subvolume root is gated on its parent: aware clients get -EACCES from check_access on the source inode, unaware clients can rename it (inferred, untested). Batching is enabled by mds_allow_batched_ops (default true). See also F-ADM-018 (per-request access checks).

features.name: Request parking for quarantine-unaware sessions
features.summary: Holds requests of clients without feature bit 24 on a quarantined subvolume inside the MDS, without reply, until the quarantine is lifted.
features.description: Server::check_quarantine_block returns false for internal requests, aware sessions and inodes not under quarantine; otherwise it adds C_MDS_RetryRequest as a WAIT_QUARANTINE waiter on the first quarantined (or being-quarantined) subvolume root up the realm chain and the caller returns without replying. Parking sites: rdlock_path_pin_ref on the target (getattr, lookup, open, readdir, setattr, setlayout, normal setxattr and removexattr, getvxattr, file locks, snapdiff, blockdiff, snapshot metadata), rdlock_path_xlock_dentry on the parent (create, mknod, mkdir, symlink, unlink, rmdir, link by ino), rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn on both parents (rename, path-based link) and handle_client_lookup_ino (lookupino, lookuphash, lookupname, lookupparent). Parked requests keep the path locks they already hold (dentry rdlocks, snaplock rdlocks up to /, and for creates parent filelock and nestlock wrlocks plus a dentry xlock) and are woken by the disable walk visiting the root or by an abort; requests woken in the first two sites are not re-checked. Kernel system calls block (killable) without timeout, and a kernel mount inside the subvolume fails with -ETIMEDOUT after mount_timeout (60 s, inferred).
features.notes: Not parked: ceph.* vxattr set/remove and SETDIRLAYOUT addressed by ino, and LOOKUPINO with a snapid; an allow * kernel client can therefore remove ceph.dir.subvolume from a quarantined root (inferred). Held locks can wedge an enable (an unaware request parked between acceptance and the root xlocks holds the root snaplock rdlock, so the command never answers and later ones get -EBUSY) and a disable with replicas; evicting the client unblocks both (inferred, untested). Parked requests are ordinary tracked ops and can raise slow-request warnings.

features.name: Snapshot operation parking under quarantine
features.summary: Parks lssnap, mksnap, rmsnap and renamesnap of unaware clients on quarantined subvolumes.
features.description: handle_client_lssnap, handle_client_mksnap, handle_client_rmsnap and handle_client_renamesnap call check_quarantine_block on the directory and re-run it on every retry, so kernel clients can neither list nor create, remove or rename snapshots (ls, mkdir, rmdir and rename in .snap) of a quarantined subvolume; commit c05f3db248a added this because kernel clients could otherwise destroy recovery snapshots. Snapdir paths are traversed without RDLOCK_PATH or RDLOCK_SNAP, so these parked requests hold no path locks. Aware clients get -EACCES from check_access instead.

features.name: Cap restriction to PIN under quarantine
features.summary: Issues only CEPH_CAP_PIN on inodes under quarantine to sessions without q/Q.
features.description: CInode::get_caps_quarantine_mask returns CEPH_CAP_PIN when the inode is under quarantine and the session lacks quarantine access for its path, and CEPH_CAP_ANY otherwise; the mask is ANDed into the any, loner and xlocker allowed masks, the careful and xlocker masks, get_caps_allowed_for_client, try_drop_loner and the snapped-inode branch of encode_inodestat, and Locker::get_allowed_caps caches the masks per q status. Directories therefore lose Fs, Fx, As, Xs and Ls too. Clients receive ordinary REVOKE messages down to PIN and flush dirty data and metadata as usual: cap flushes and releases are not gated, dentry leases are not restricted, and OSD access is untouched (a client that already holds valid caps or writes objects directly with its OSD caps is not stopped, inferred).
features.notes: Caps issued before a change persist until the next evaluation (walk, lock change, cap request, reissue_all_caps). The cap walk does not proactively revoke caps on the .meta file, but any later issue_caps restricts them.

features.name: EQUARANTINED errno in MClientCaps
features.summary: Tags cap grants and revokes on quarantined inodes with oserrno -1000 for sessions without q/Q.
features.description: MClientCaps HEAD_VERSION 14 appends int32 oserrno after subvolume_id. In Locker::issue_caps, every CEPH_CAP_OP_GRANT or REVOKE built by the main issue/revoke branch for an inode under quarantine carries -EQUARANTINED (EQUARANTINED = 1000) for sessions without q/Q and 0 for sessions with it; the stale-cap re-issue branch, cap import/export and flush acks never set it, and -EQUARANTINED is never a request result. The C++ client marks an inode quarantined on a revoke with -EQUARANTINED and clears the mark on a grant beyond PIN with oserrno 0; the kernel decodes MClientCaps only up to its v12 fields and ignores oserrno.

features.name: QUARANTINE marker in InodeStat
features.summary: Marks the quarantined subvolume root in replies with an optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE.
features.description: encode_inodestat adds an optmetadata entry of kind QUARANTINE (2) when the inode itself has the persisted flag (only the subvolume root), with a default quarantine_md_t (enabled true, timestamp 0: the real time is not sent); descendants carry no marker. It is emitted inside InodeStat v9 (sessions with CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING) between fscrypt_file and subvolume_id. libcephfs stores optmetadata verbatim and its Inode::is_under_quarantine walks client-side parents for this marker or a -EQUARANTINED cap errno; the kernel skips optmetadata as an opaque versioned blob.

features.name: MQuarantineDisable notification
features.summary: When the quarantine code sends MQuarantineDisable.
features.description: See F-PROTO-097 for the message. Quarantine-specific: on disable the cap-revocation walk sends it to every quarantine-aware session holding a cap on each visited inode, and the QUARANTINE_INODE finisher sends it once more for the root; directories whose walk op had children get it twice. The C++ client's handle_quarantine_disable clears its quarantine mark and signals cap waiters.
features.notes: See also F-QOS-064 (cap-revocation walk), F-QOS-075 (EQUARANTINED errno).

features.name: MDS self-authentication, keyring and rotating service secrets
features.summary: The MDS authenticates to the monitors as `mds.<id>` and obtains service tickets and rotating `mds` secrets so that it can talk to mons, OSDs, peer MDSs and the mgr and verify client authorizers.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::init` sets `want_keys` to MON|OSD|MDS|MGR, installs the `MonClient` as the messenger's AuthClient and AuthServer, calls `authenticate()` and then `wait_auth_rotating(rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout)` up to `max_rotating_auth_attempts` times; failure of either step calls `suicide()`. The default `keyring` for an MDS is `$mds_data/keyring` (`/var/lib/ceph/mds/$cluster-$id/keyring`), set by `common_preinit`; without a loadable key cephx is dropped from the supported methods and init fails with `-ENOENT` unless `none` is configured. The monitor hands out three rotating secrets per service (previous, current, next); the MDS keeps only the last set and requests a new one when fewer than three are held or the current one expired at least `min(30 s, auth_service_ticket_ttl/4)` ago. Methods and modes towards mon/mgr follow `auth_cluster_required` and `ms_mon_cluster_mode`, towards MDS/OSD `auth_cluster_required` and `ms_cluster_mode`, towards clients `auth_service_required` and `ms_service_mode`. The peers enforce the MDS entity's own caps: deployed as `mon 'profile mds'` (beacons need `mds` X, eviction needs `osd blocklist`, `MRemoveSnaps` needs `osd pool rmsnap`), `osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*'` and `mds 'allow'` (a peer MDS refuses a connection whose `mds` cap is missing).
features.notes: cephadm writes the keyring into the daemon data directory mounted at `/var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>`; Rook passes `--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring` explicitly, gives the MDS `osd 'allow *'` instead of the `cephfs` tag, and with AES256K support the key and rotating secrets are `aes256k` (rook f190ca3b45f; see the mgr-tools page 3.9.3). The mgr accepts MDS connections even with empty mgr caps (`DaemonServer::ms_handle_fast_authentication`). See also F-PROTO-012 (rotating secrets as clients depend on them), F-CLU-110 (MonClient session and subscriptions).

features.name: Peer authorizer verification and caps loading at connection accept
features.summary: Every connecting peer is authenticated with a cephx authorizer for service type MDS, and the `mds` caps carried in its ticket become the session's `auth_caps`.
features.description: The authorizer itself is verified by `MonClient::handle_auth_request` with the rotating `mds` secret (F-PROTO-011). `MDSDaemon::ms_handle_fast_authentication` then parses the caps from the ticket on the messenger worker without `mds_lock` (`parse_caps`: allow_all -> allow-all, else decode one string and run `MDSAuthCaps::parse`); an entity with no `mds` cap (empty blob, decode throws) or an unparseable string refuses the connection with `-EACCES`, which the peer sees as BADAUTHORIZER (msgr1) or `AUTH_BAD_METHOD` (msgr2) (or `_exit(auth_exit_on_failure)` when that option is >= 0). `ms_handle_accept` then finds the existing `Session` for `entity_name_t(peer_type, global_id)` or creates a closed one (also on a rank-less daemon, so that `allow *` peers can run tell commands) and parses the caps again into `Session::auth_caps`. The caps are a snapshot taken when the ticket was issued; they are never persisted: `session_info_t` keeps only `auth_name`, and sessions loaded from the SessionMap or created by import have empty caps until the client connects.
features.notes: Caps refresh only with a new `Connection` object: a msgr2 reconnect merged by `ProtocolV2::reuse_connection` (stateful_server policy) moves the socket and `auth_meta` but not `peer_caps_info`, so `ms_handle_accept` re-parses the old caps (code reading, not reproduced; src/msg/async/ProtocolV2.cc:2814). The kclient on `AUTH_BAD_METHOD` invalidates its MDS ticket and returns `-EACCES` (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7363 (mds_handle_auth_bad_method)). The transport and handshake themselves belong to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol. No code compares the claimed entity type with the type of the authenticated EntityName (transport page 3.2). MCommand (ceph tell) on a client connection requires auth_caps.allow_all() (F-ADM-028). See also F-PROTO-011 (authorizer), F-PROTO-015 (connection-to-session binding).

legacy_parts.note: The msgr1 refusal path: -EACCES from ms_handle_fast_authentication answered with CEPH_MSGR_TAG_BADAUTHORIZER by ProtocolV1::handle_connect_message_2. The gates cephx_require_signatures and cephx_service_require_version, which the accepting daemon evaluates only in ProtocolV1::handle_connect_message_2, where they add CEPH_FEATURE_MSG_AUTH and CEPH_FEATUREMASK_CEPHX_V2 to the msgr1 required features. Only a peer connected over msgr1 receives the refusal as BADAUTHORIZER and is subject to the signature and cephx-version gates. The 7.3 kernel mounted by mount.ceph with the new device syntax runs with ms_mode=prefer-crc, and Ceph clients and daemons at this commit connect to the first usable address of the MDS addrvec, which daemons publish v2 first, so a refused baseline peer receives AUTH_BAD_METHOD over msgr2. Message signatures exist only in ProtocolV1; the kernel's msgr1 default applies only to the old device syntax or an explicit ms_mode=legacy.
evidence_notes: grep of src: cephx_require_signatures, cephx_service_require_signatures and cephx_*require_version are read only in src/msg/async/ProtocolV1.cc and src/mon/AuthMonitor.cc

features.name: Authentication method none (and Kerberos) means allow-all
features.summary: Without cephx for clients, every client peer is treated as holding `mds 'allow *'`, including for tell commands.
features.description: With `auth_service_required = none`, `AuthNoneAuthorizeHandler::verify_authorizer` sets `AuthCapsInfo::allow_all = true`; `MDSDaemon::parse_caps` then calls `MDSAuthCaps::set_allow_all()`, which installs one grant with spec `ALL` and an empty match. The Kerberos handler does the same (`KrbAuthorizeHandler.cpp:50`). The entity name and global id are taken from the peer's unauthenticated claim. Daemon peers follow `auth_cluster_required`. Under cephx a service ticket never carries `allow_all` (`cephx_verify_authorizer` rejects it).

features.name: Peer-type message filtering and rank address check
features.summary: Security view of message filtering: which peer may send what, and what is not bound to the authenticated identity.
features.description: See F-CLU-115 (dispatch and peer-type filtering) and F-CLU-072 (stale peer messages). Security-relevant facts: MSG_COMMAND is not type-filtered (it is gated by allow_all()); client session, reconnect, reclaim, caps, cap-release and lease messages are accepted only from CLIENT peers; CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REQUEST is not type-filtered, but a session is attached only when req->is_a_client(), and Server::check_access is a no-op for session-less requests; inter-rank messages are accepted only from MDS peers whose rank is up and only on the connection to that rank's MDSMap address. The MDS never forwards an MClientRequest itself (it sends MClientRequestForward to the client), so each request is evaluated against the caps of the connection it arrived on.
features.notes: Peer type and message source are not bound to the authenticated entity: on the accepting side `ProtocolV2::handle_hello` takes the peer type from the HELLO frame and the source from CLIENT_IDENT; no comparison with the authenticated `peer_name`/`peer_global_id` was found (code search; not reproduced; auth page section 8 item 25).

features.name: Daemon key rotation commands (rotate-key, wipe-rotating-secrets)
features.summary: The MDS process accepts a new cephx key for its own entity through an admin command; cephadm has a (currently uncalled) rotation path that uses it.
features.description: `MonClient::init` registers the asok/tell commands `rotate-key` (input buffer = base64 key, added for the daemon's own entity to the in-memory keyring; `-EINVAL` on decode failure or without cephx) and `wipe-rotating-secrets`. The tell is subject to the `allow *` gate. The monitor side of a rotation is `auth get-or-create-pending` / `auth commit-pending`. cephadm's `_rotate_daemon_key` (pending key, keyring rewrite, `rotate-key` tell, restart on failure) has no caller at this commit: `ceph orch daemon rotate-key` fails with "key rotation by orchestrator not supported in this release". Rook rotates with the mon command `auth rotate`, rewrites the keyring Secret and restarts the pod; it never sends `rotate-key`.
features.notes: During a cephadm upgrade an MDS named in `AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE` gets its key rotated with `mgr.key_rotate` before redeploy (src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/upgrade.py:1917-1975).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: MDS cap string grammar, parser and canonical forms
features.summary: Parses the `mds` cap string of an entity into grants; the monitor validates cap strings with the same C++ parser, so the accepted language is shared.
features.description: Grammar (Boost.Spirit, no skipper inside): grants `allow <spec> [fsname=F] [path=P] [root_squash] [uid=N] [gids=a,b,...] [network CIDR]` separated by `,` or `;` with only spaces around the separator; `spec` is `*`, `all`, or `r` followed by optional `w f p Q q s` in exactly this order; qualifiers in exactly this order; the complete string `allow` (byte-exact) means `allow rwps`. Keywords are case-sensitive; unquoted paths are limited to `[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]`, quoted paths cannot contain their quote character; `fsname=*` is not expressible; `uid` is a 32-bit unsigned decimal; `network` is separated by a space, not `=`. On failure all grants are cleared and the error text is "Permission flags in MDS capability string must be '*' or 'all' or must start with 'r'" (remainder contains `allow`) or "mds capability parse failed, stopped at '<rest>' of '<str>'". `operator<<` prints `allow <spec>[ fsname=F][ path="/P"][ root_squash][ uid=U[ gids=..]][ network N]`; `to_string()` (used by the monitor's merge) prints the path without leading slash and quotes and omits `network`.
features.notes: Whitespace quirks confirmed in a standalone harness against Boost 1.83: leading/trailing `ascii::space` of the whole string is skipped (`" allow r "` parses) but `" allow"` and `"allow "` fail because the legacy compare is byte-exact. `gids=` without `uid=` parses and has no effect. Uids >= 2^31 parse but never match (caller uid compared as `int`). A bracketed IPv6 network parses but yields an unusable grant. With `mon_auth_validate_all_caps=false` an invalid string can enter the auth database and is then refused by the MDS at connection time.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: Grant evaluation: union of grants in a fixed step order
features.summary: Decides whether a request with a given access mask on an inode is allowed for a session; any passing grant allows, otherwise the client gets `-EACCES`.
features.description: `MDSAuthCaps::is_capable` iterates grants in string order: (1) skip if the grant has a network and the session address is outside it or the network is invalid; (2) skip unless fs name, uid/gids and path match; (3) skip unless the spec allows the read/execute and write bits of the mask; (4) if a quarantine check is requested and the grant lacks `q`/`Q`, return false immediately; (5) skip a `root_squash` grant for `MAY_WRITE` when caller uid or gid is 0; (6) skip if `MAY_SET_VXATTR`, `MAY_SNAPSHOT` or `MAY_FULL` is requested and the grant lacks `p`, `s` or `f`; (7) allow if the grant uid is ANY; (8) otherwise apply the chown/chgrp rules and the owner/group/other mode-bit test. There are no deny grants; only step 4 makes the result order-dependent. Mask bits: `MAY_READ` 1, `MAY_WRITE` 2, `MAY_EXECUTE` 4 (never requested), `MAY_CHOWN` 16, `MAY_CHGRP` 32, `MAY_SET_VXATTR` 64, `MAY_SNAPSHOT` 128, `MAY_FULL` 256. Spec `*`/`all` implies `r w f p s` but never `q`/`Q`.
features.notes: Evaluation is a pure function of (session caps, inode path, inode uid/gid/mode, caller credentials, mask, peer address). Worked examples and the unit tests (`src/test/mds/TestMDSAuthCaps.cc`) are on the auth page section 3.5. Clients evaluate the exported `cap_auths` with different semantics (last matching grant wins, no match allows), see F-ADM-021.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: path= restriction and the inode path used for checks
features.summary: Restricts a grant to a subtree; the MDS compares the inode's primary path from the file-system root with the grant path.
features.description: At parse time all leading `/` of the grant path are stripped; trailing `/` are ignored by `match_path`; an empty path (also `path=/` or `path=""`) matches everything; otherwise the inode path must equal the grant path or continue with `/` (`path=/foo` matches `foo`, `foo/d`, not `food`). Inner `//`, `.` and `..` are not normalized. `Session::check_access` builds the projected primary-parent path with `make_path_string` and strips the leading `/`; for an inode whose parent is a stray directory it uses the inode's `stray_prior_path` (set at unlink and when rename unlinks a target), and the parent's `stray_prior_path` when the grandparent is a stray (inode inside a deleted snapshotted directory). The uid, gid and mode compared later come from the committed (non-projected) inode. Access through a remote (hard) link is judged by the primary link's path.
features.notes: mgr/volumes (`allow r|rw path=<subvolume data path>`), mgr/nfs (`allow rw path=<export path>`) and `ceph fs authorize` all produce path grants. The path is the only non-local input of the check, so a rename of any ancestor changes the result.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: fsname= restriction and file-system gating of session messages
features.summary: Restricts a grant to one file system and refuses session traffic for file systems the entity has no grant for.
features.description: `MDSCapMatch::match_fs` treats `""` or `"*"` as any file system. `fs_name_capable(fs, MAY_READ)` (true for `allow_all()` or any grant for the fs whose spec allows read; ignores path, uid and network) is checked for every `MClientSession` when the MDSMap has an fs name: on failure the MDS sends `CEPH_SESSION_REJECT` with `metadata["error_string"] = client doesn't have caps for FS "<fs>"` directly on the connection. `MClientReclaim` failing the same test is silently dropped. libcephfs surfaces a REJECT as `-EPERM` ("Operation not permitted" at mount); the kclient fails later requests with `-EACCES` unless mounted with `recover_session=clean`.
features.notes: `ceph fs rename` does not rewrite `fsname=` caps and requires `--yes-i-really-mean-it` because "clients' cephx credentials need reauthorized" (src/mon/FSCommands.cc:1336). Reconnect messages are not fs-name checked (`Server::handle_client_reconnect`). The kclient compares fs names with `ceph_namespace_match` (`NULL`, `""`, `"*"` match any).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: uid=/gids= restriction with simplified mode-bit check
features.summary: Limits a grant to an asserted caller uid (and groups) and then checks the inode's owner/group/other permission bits for that caller.
features.description: A grant with `uid=N` matches only requests whose `caller_uid` equals N and, if `gids` are given, whose `caller_gid` or a supplementary gid (from `MClientRequest` `gid_list`) is listed. After the flag checks, the class is owner if `inode_uid == caller_uid`, else group if `inode_gid` is in the grant gids held by the caller, else other; the class's r/w/x bits must cover the mask. `MAY_CHOWN` requires `new_uid == caller_uid` and `inode_uid == caller_uid` (never both true, because setattr adds `MAY_CHOWN` only when the uid changes, so a uid grant never allows chown); `MAY_CHGRP` requires ownership and a new gid in the effective gid set. The caller identity is asserted by the client and not verified by the MDS. Open for write requests `MAY_READ` too (except an `O_TRUNC` open), and getattr/lookup need `MAY_READ` on the target.
features.notes: `uid=0` is stored as -1 (any), so a grant cannot be restricted to root. `std::set_intersection` assumes a sorted `caller_gid_list`, which the MDS uses as received (kclient lists are sorted; libcephfs and Ganesha lists are passed as supplied, unverified whether sorted). No mgr module or orchestrator generates `uid=` grants (none found in the map pages).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: root_squash grants
features.summary: A `root_squash` grant cannot be used for writes by callers with uid 0 or gid 0.
features.description: In `is_capable` step 5, a grant with `root_squash` is skipped (not denied) when `caller_uid == 0` or `caller_gid == 0` and the mask contains `MAY_WRITE`; another grant may still allow. Vxattr operations request only `MAY_SET_VXATTR` (no `MAY_WRITE`), so `allow rwp root_squash` lets root set quotas, layouts and pins. `root_squash_in_caps(fs)` feeds the broken-root_squash health check, and the flag is exported to clients in `cap_auths` for client-side enforcement of cached operations. `ceph fs authorize ... root_squash` and the dashboard generate it; the monitor's merge can add `root_squash` to a grant but never remove it.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: p flag: permission to set ceph.* vxattrs and non-default layouts
features.summary: Gates changes of layouts, quotas, pins, subvolume flags, charmap and quiesce-block vxattrs.
features.description: `MAY_SET_VXATTR` is requested (alone, without `MAY_WRITE`) by `handle_client_setvxattr` for SETXATTR/RMXATTR of `is_ceph_vxattr` names (`ceph.dir.layout*`, `ceph.file.layout*`, `ceph.quota*`, `ceph.quiesce.block`, `ceph.dir.subvolume`, `ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible`, `ceph.dir.pin`, `.pin.random`, `.pin.distributed`, `ceph.dir.charmap`, `.normalization`, `.encoding`, `.casesensitive`). It is added to `MAY_WRITE` for SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT that change the layout and for CREATE whose requested stripe unit/count, object size or pool differ from the inherited layout. A failing grant is skipped; with no passing grant the request gets `-EACCES`.
features.notes: `allow rp` (accepted by the MDS grammar, rejected by `ceph fs authorize`) can set layouts, quotas and pins without write permission. mgr/volumes and mgr/mirroring rely on their mounts holding `p` (mgr has `allow *`; mirror bootstrap generates `rwps`).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: s flag and snapshot uid range
features.summary: Gates mksnap, rmsnap and renamesnap; a separate uid range option gates all snapshot-modifying ops.
features.description: MKSNAP (0x1400), RMSNAP (0x1401) and RENAMESNAP (0x1403) call `check_access(MAY_WRITE|MAY_SNAPSHOT)` on the directory; before that, a caller uid outside [`mds_snap_min_uid`, `mds_snap_max_uid`] returns `-EPERM`. SNAP_METADATA (0x1406) applies only the uid range and has no caps check, so an `allow r` client (the cephfs-mirror daemon) can update snapshot metadata. LSSNAP and READDIR_SNAPDIFF request `MAY_READ`.
features.notes: Snapshot semantics themselves (realms, snap ids, limits) belong to category 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. See also F-SNAP-020 (uid range option).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: f flag: metadata-pool-full bypass
features.summary: The f flag of an MDS cap grant bypasses the metadata-pool-full gate.
features.description: See F-STORE-099. Auth-cap specifics: a grant with f (or *) satisfies the MAY_FULL check that dispatch_client_request makes on the request's base inode while the metadata pool is full; without it the request fails (clients see -EACCES from check_access). The f bypass does not apply to a SETATTR that grows a file while full, which returns -ENOSPC regardless.
features.notes: `ceph fs authorize` cannot generate `f` ("Unknown permission flag 'f'"). Double reply derived from code reading, not reproduced.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: q/Q flags: access to quarantined subtrees
features.summary: Grants with `q` or `Q` keep access to quarantined subvolumes; other quarantine-aware sessions are denied there.
features.description: For clients advertising `CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE`, `Server::check_access` passes `check_qtine = in->is_under_quarantine()`; the first grant that matches fs, path, uid and r/w but lacks `q`/`Q` returns false (`-EACCES`) without consulting later grants. `quarantine_access_in_caps(fs, path)` is evaluated by `Locker::issue_new_caps`/`issue_caps` for each client cap on every issue, restricting caps on quarantined inodes. `Q` is documented as access to all quarantined subtrees but is evaluated exactly like `q` (limited by the grant path). Neither is implied by `*`/`all`.
features.notes: The inode path is built for every cap issue even without quarantine (only the `EQUARANTINED` errno path is gated on `is_under_quarantine()`). The quarantine mechanism itself belongs to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. Grammar: after r the optional letters come in the fixed order w f p Q q s (for example rwq, rwQ, rq, rwfpQqs) and are printed in that order; in MDSCapSpec Q = 1<<6 and Q_PRIME = 1<<7. For requests, MDSAuthCaps::is_capable lets the first grant that matches network, fs, path, uid and r/w decide; for caps, quarantine_access_in_caps is true if any grant with a matching fs name has q or Q and a path equal to the inode path or an ancestor, ignoring uid/gid, network and root_squash. First-match pitfall: with "allow rw, allow rwq path=/volumes/_nogroup/sv", requests on sv get -EACCES (the first grant lacks q) while issue_caps grants full caps. The monitor validates cap strings with the same parser and distributes them in tickets. See also F-QOS-071 (EACCES for aware sessions), F-QOS-074 (cap restriction).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: network restriction
features.summary: A grant with `network A/P` applies only to sessions whose peer address lies inside that CIDR.
features.description: The session's `info.inst.addr` is tested with `network_contains` (same address family required); `parse_network` needs `addr/prefix` accepted by `inet_pton`, and a grant whose network does not parse is unusable in `is_capable`. The network is ignored by `allow_all()` (tell and fscrypt gates), `fs_name_capable` and `path_capable`, and is dropped by `to_string()`, so a `ceph fs authorize` merge loses it.
features.notes: Unit test `network`: `allow * network 192.168.0.0/16, allow * network 10.0.0.0/8` denies a client at 192.167.2.3.

features.name: Mount root check at session open and auth_name check at reclaim
features.summary: At `REQUEST_OPEN` the client-claimed mount root must be covered by some grant path; reclaiming another session requires the same cephx entity.
features.description: In `handle_client_session` for `CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_OPEN`, after the `refuse_client_session`, blocklist and required-feature checks and the root_squash detection, a `root` metadata key (if present) must start with `/` and satisfy `path_capable` (a textual prefix test that ignores fs name, spec and network); failure sends `CEPH_SESSION_REJECT` with `error_string` `invalue root '<root>'` (sic) or `non-allowable root '<root>'` (only to clients with `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC`) and clog warning `client session with ... denied`. The kclient sends `root` = mount server path or `/`; libcephfs sends its mount root (`/` by default) but omits the key outside `mount` (`mds_command` on an unmounted client, `start_reclaim`), which skips the check. `Server::reclaim_session` refuses with `MClientReclaimReply` result `-EPERM` when `session->info.auth_name` differs from the target's; `auth_name` is persisted in `session_info_t` and `ESession` for this purpose.
features.notes: The root test is a convenience gate (`/a/../b` passes `path=/a`); reconnect re-checks neither fs name nor root. Caps `allow r fsname=a path=/a, allow rw fsname=b path=/b` let a client open a session on fs `a` with root `/b`, after which every checked operation is denied. Session state machinery belongs to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol. See also F-PROTO-029 (session open admission).

legacy_parts.note: REJECT for an invalid or non-allowable root sent to a session without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8): send_reject_message omits error_string, so MClientSession is encoded as header v1. Sessions without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8) come only from kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1, whose feature sets are inferred and never include bit 8. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bit 8, so a refused root reaches them as a header-v7 REJECT that carries error_string.
evidence: linux-v4.18/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:953 (create_session_open_msg, session v2 without feature bits)

features.name: Per-request access-check matrix
features.summary: Defines which inode and which mask each client operation is checked against, and which operations are not checked.
features.description: `Server::check_access(mdr, in, mask)` is a no-op without a session, else calls `Session::check_access`, which returns `-EIO` for a directory whose layout has a pool namespace when the connection lacks `CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2`, then `-EACCES` if `is_capable` fails. Targets and masks: LOOKUP/GETATTR/LOOKUPSNAP `MAY_READ` on the target; LOOKUPINO/HASH/PARENT/NAME mask 0 on the target (match only) then `MAY_READ` on the parent if locks were requested; OPEN `MAY_READ` plus `MAY_WRITE` for write modes (`O_TRUNC` checks `MAY_WRITE` only); CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK `MAY_WRITE` on the parent; READDIR `MAY_READ`; SETATTR `MAY_WRITE` (+`MAY_CHOWN`/`MAY_CHGRP` when uid/gid change); SETXATTR of non-ceph names `MAY_WRITE`; LINK target and destination dir, UNLINK/RMDIR parent only, RENAME source dir, destination dir and source inode, each `MAY_WRITE` on the first pass only (skipped once peers witnessed). Not checked: RMXATTR of non-`ceph.*` names, GETVXATTR, SETFILELOCK/GETFILELOCK, FILE_BLOCKDIFF, SNAP_METADATA (uid range only). Most checks run after path traversal and lock acquisition, under `mds_lock`.
features.notes: Batched getattr/lookup (`mds_allow_batched_ops`): only the batch head runs `check_access`, and `Batch_Getattr_Lookup::_respond` sends its result and trace to followers from other sessions. Cap flushes (`MClientCaps` with dirty metadata) are not access-checked since commit 96305b5eef0. `Server::_check_access` is declared in Server.h:234 and never defined. The full table with line numbers is on the auth page section 3.7. See also F-QOS-071 (quarantine EACCES).

legacy_parts.note: The -EIO return of Session::check_access for a directory whose layout has a pool namespace when the connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2. The declaration Server::_check_access, which has no definition and no caller. A connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (bit 58) only for kernels before v4.5 and Ceph clients before 10.2.0. The 7.3 kernel advertises bit 58 (under its aliases CRUSH_TUNABLES5 and NEW_OSDOPREPLY_ENCODING) in its msgr2 client ident, and libcephfs at this commit includes FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 in CEPH_FEATURES_ALL, so baseline sessions go straight to is_capable. Server::_check_access is declared in Server.h and is neither defined nor called in src/mds.
evidence_notes: grep of src/mds finds no definition or call)

features.name: fscrypt attribute changes require allow *
features.summary: Setting the fscrypt auth or file attributes through SETATTR is allowed only for sessions whose caps satisfy `allow_all()`.
features.description: After the regular `check_access(MAY_WRITE)` of SETATTR, a request carrying `CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_FILE` or `CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_AUTH` returns `-EACCES` unless `session->auth_caps.allow_all()` (a `*` grant without path and uid; fs name and network ignored). `fscrypt_auth`/`fscrypt_file` sent with a create are copied into the new inode in `prepare_new_inode` without this gate.
features.notes: mgr/volumes copies `ceph.fscrypt.auth`/`ceph.fscrypt.file` when creating clones; libcephfs turns those setxattrs into SETATTR with the fscrypt flags (mgr-tools page 3.1.4). See also F-NS-064, F-CACHE-009.

features.name: cap_auths export in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN and client-side checks
features.summary: Every session OPEN message carries a reduced copy of the session's grants so that clients can enforce read-only and root_squash for operations they complete from cached caps.
features.description: Each `MClientSession` with op `CEPH_SESSION_OPEN` carries `vector<MDSCapAuth>` in grant order: per grant `MDSCapMatch` v1 (s64 uid with -1 = any, u32 count + u32 gids, string path without leading `/`, string fs_name, u8 root_squash) plus u8 `readable` and u8 `writeable`, each struct with a 6-byte versioned header. It is on the wire only for message version >= 6, which is used when `metadata` or `supported_features` is non-empty (the MDS fills `supported_features` only for `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC` clients); `HEAD_VERSION = 7` appends `oldest_client_tid`. Sent from `_session_logged`, the already-open re-notification (REQUEST_OPEN with `CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE`), `finish_force_open_sessions` (import, rejoin, cross-MDS rename) and reconnect success. The kclient replaces its mount-wide list on every OPEN from any rank and checks `ceph_open`, `ceph_atomic_open` (parent path), unlink/rmdir/rmsnap and setattr; libcephfs checks `_do_setattr` and cap-satisfied `_open`. Client semantics: the last matching grant decides; no match allows; `p`, `s`, `f`, `q`, network and mode bits are unknown to clients.
features.notes: The kclient reads the fields positionally after skipping the 6-byte headers without using `len` (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4468-4527), so the v1 field layout is fixed for it. An OPEN built by `finish_force_open_sessions` before the client connected is queued with an empty list (imported sessions have empty `auth_caps`), which disables kclient checks until a later OPEN (derived from code reading). Example of the semantic split: caps `allow rw, allow r path=/ro` let the MDS allow writes in `/ro` while the kclient refuses write opens there. Client versions: Linux v6.10+, Ceph 18.2.4 and 19.2.0+ advertise bit 21; kernels v6.8-v6.9 already send session v7 but do not parse cap_auths, and an OPEN below v6 clears the kernel list. Because the kernel ignores struct_len here, any field appended to MDSCapAuth or MDSCapMatch desynchronizes every kernel that parses cap_auths (kclient expectations 8). libcephfs never tests the MDS bit 21, allows access locally when no grant matches or no list was sent, and sends cap flushes with caller_uid/gid -1. See also F-PROTO-031 (MClientSession encoding), F-ADM-022.

legacy_parts.note: OPEN sent to a session without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8): all four OPEN send sites leave supported_features and metric_spec empty for such a session, so MClientSession::encode_payload emits header v1, which has no cap_auths field. Only kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1 open sessions without bit 8, so only they receive an OPEN without the feature bitmap and without cap_auths. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bit 8 and bit 21, so every OPEN they receive is header v7 and carries cap_auths.
evidence: linux-v4.18/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:953 (create_session_open_msg, session v2 without feature bits)

features.name: MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH health check
features.summary: Raises a HEALTH_ERR check for sessions whose caps use root_squash but whose client cannot enforce it locally.
features.description: At `REQUEST_OPEN` and at reconnect, a session whose caps contain `root_squash` for this fs and whose client lacks `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK` (bit 21) is added to `SessionMap::broken_root_squash_clients`; the session is not rejected. `Beacon::notify_health` reports metric `MDS_HEALTH_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH` (id 15, check code `MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH`, HEALTH_ERR): one metric per client ("Client <name> has broken root_squash implementation", metadata `client_id`) or, above `mds_health_summarize_threshold` (10), one summary metric "There are N clients with broken root_squash implementations" (metadata `client_count`). Summary: "%num% MDS report clients with broken root_squash implementation". Entries are removed only by `SessionMap::remove_session`.
features.notes: The set holds raw `Session*`; a session added at REQUEST_OPEN and then rejected is never removed and may be dereferenced after free by the next `notify_health` (code reading, not reproduced; auth page section 8 item 17). Because the check is HEALTH_ERR and not on Rook's ignore list, it stops Rook's CephFilesystem reconcile while raised (mgr-tools page 3.9.2). Affected clients: kernels before v6.10 and Ceph clients before 18.2.4/19.2.0 (kclient expectations 7.1.2). See also F-ADM-021 (client-side checks), F-ADM-011 (root_squash).

legacy.note: The check is raised only for a session whose caps use root_squash on the file system and whose client lacks CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK (bit 21): Linux before v6.10 (including the CentOS Stream 8 sample) and Ceph clients before 18.2.4 and 19.2.0. The 7.3 kernel advertises bit 21, and libcephfs at this commit advertises CEPHFS_FEATURES_ALL for ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha V15.7, cephfs-mirror and the mgr modules, so no baseline client triggers it. Only the debug option client_debug_inject_features can remove the bit from libcephfs.
evidence_notes: git show v18.2.2/v18.2.4:src/mds/cephfs_features.h (bit 21 absent in 18.2.2, present in 18.2.4)

features.group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
features.name: ceph fs authorize: cap generation and merge on the monitor
features.summary: The monitor command that generates matching mon/mds/osd caps for a client and merges new grants into existing ones.
features.description: `ceph fs authorize <fs|*|all> <entity> <path> <perm> [root_squash] [<path> <perm> [root_squash] ...]`: unknown fs gives `-EINVAL`; perm characters must be strictly increasing ASCII except the leading `rw`, allowed `r w p s q Q` and `*` alone, `f` rejected. Generated strings: mon `allow r[ fsname=<fs>]`; mds `allow <perm>[ fsname=<fs>][ path=<path>][ root_squash]` per pair joined with `", "` (no `path=` for `/`, path unquoted); osd `allow r[w] tag cephfs data=<fs>`.
